# Contract benchmark results

<!-- Generated by scripts/run_contract_bench.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Each of the specimen defects in a category Mumei targets has a requirement and one contract (requires/ensures) that the buggy and the fixed function are both checked against. The right answer is: buggy version refuted, fixed version proven. Values are medians over runs, with the range in brackets.

| Arm | Model | Runs | Buggy refuted | Fixed proven | Both right | Buggy accepted | Fixed rejected | Inconclusive | Cost |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| mumei (reference ports) | — | 1 | 71 / 71 | 69 / 71 | 69 | 0 | 2 | 0 | — |

The reference ports were written by hand with knowledge of the defects, so the first row shows that the contracts can express each requirement and that the checker tells the two versions apart. It is not a detection result. The LLM rows are the comparison: the model sees only the product source file and the requirement.

Vacuity control (fixed port re-checked with `ensures: false`, must fail): 71 / 71 pass.

Reference cases where mumei did not give the right answer:

- `PY01-D08` (python, `subcategory`): buggy refuted, fixed refuted — Verification Error: Potential Out-of-Bounds on 'parts' (index may be < 0 or >= len_parts)
- `PY02-D04` (python, `parse_row`): buggy refuted, fixed refuted — Verification Error: Potential Out-of-Bounds on 'row' (index may be < 0 or >= len_row)
